strategy.positioning: The running brand that publishes the complete, audited footprint of every shoe it makes — proof before promises, for runners who read labels the way they read splits.
strategy.key_message: Don't take our word for it. Read the receipt.
pillars: Radical receipts: every material, cost and emission itemized and independently audited
Performance parity: verified against category benchmarks before any sustainability claim is made
Public accountability: misses and failures published alongside the wins
strategy.rationale: Research shows the audience is data-literate and distrustful by default; competitors either lead with vague green language (attackable) or bury their proof (forgettable). Owning verifiable transparency converts the audience's skepticism from a barrier into the buying trigger itself.

big_idea: The Living Receipt: every pair ships with its audited, itemized footprint printed on the tongue and living at a public URL — and at mile 500 the receipt gets a second page: swap the outsole and midsole core with a rebuild kit and keep the same shoe on the books.

copy.headline: Stop buying new shoes.
copy.subhead: Every pair publishes its audited footprint — materials, emissions, and the misses — where you can't avoid it.
copy.body: Most brands print a slogan on the tongue. We print the bill: 4.9 kg CO2e, 61% recycled upper, zero offsets, audited by people we can't fire. When a number improves, we update it. When it gets worse, we publish that too. You wouldn't train on vibes — don't buy on them either.

rationale: The Living Receipt: every pair ships with its audited, itemized footprint printed on the tongue and living at a public URL — and at mile 500 the receipt gets a second page: swap the outsole and midsole core with a rebuild kit and keep the same shoe on the books. — Don't take our word for it. Read the receipt.
